placements.why: This envelope establishes a standing operational practice (monthly rollback rehearsals, formally owned) that is organizational in nature rather than a product, architecture, or opportunity concern. No existing strata category is supplied to hold organizational-practice mandates, and the content's shape — a recurring cadence with a named owner — matches the taxonomy's known 'Organization' category style, so it is minted fresh rather than folded into something ill-fitting.
placements.title: Operational rehearsal discipline becomes its own organizational category
placements.frame: What recurring operational commitments and accountability structures does this category need to hold?

placements.title: Rehearsal is the condition that makes rollback capability real
placements.frame: Does the expression treat performed, recurring rehearsal as what actually constitutes an operational capability, as opposed to an assumed or theoretical one?
placements.why: Quinton's directive (src-1) states the governing principle directly: an unrehearsed rollback is not a real rollback. The recorded cadence (src-3) and named owner (src-4) are the concrete facts that operationalize that principle into a standing monthly practice with accountability attached — they evidence the theme rather than stand as themes of their own. Nothing in the supplied graph structure exists yet to hold this (it is empty), and the theme is one future envelopes about rehearsal drills, resilience testing, or capability verification will plausibly keep feeding, so it is mint rather than a one-off fact.
